result:
Lane closed out. Attempt 1 had actually done all the science — it just ended in draft.

**State when I resumed:** PR #186 draft, CI green on `ecd4b4d38f`, the `[lane.swatchorder50]` verdict already posted to #50 at 16:13:57Z, NOTES.md written, `Files:` already matching the diff. The only thing missing was the mark-ready, plus the resume's ask for a written reason the first attempt stopped.

**What I did, and nothing more:**
- Added a *Why attempt 1 did not finish* section to `docs/lanes/swatchorder50/NOTES.md:14` — it finished the work and ended silently in draft while CI was still running, leaving the PR in the one state `board.sh`, `fleet.py` and `fold.sh` all skip, with no `waiting:` comment saying why.
- Merged `origin/master` (`1e184b134f`) — clean, and the 13 intervening commits touch no file this lane wrote. Since the notes commit made a new head anyway, this costs the same single CI run rather than leaving the PR 13 behind for the fold.
- `docs/testing/preflight.sh` passes on the branch (territory, coverage, board files all ok).
- `gh pr ready 186` — head `e2375a9794`, draft=false.
- Posted a `[lane.swatchorder50] done:` comment recording the above.

**The verdict itself is unchanged and not re-derived:** neither reading. Readings 1 and 2 are bit-identical in RGB to stack A's render target and differ only in alpha (255 vs the measured 221/0xDD), so the existing captures already separate them from the aliasing model without a disc variant — 1119/1120 for aliasing, 9/1120 for either reading, with the goldens column inverting it exactly.

Definition of done: all five items met. `nv2a_issues.toml` untouched — issue.50's `status_note` is left for the board, as the brief requires. Prediction is `none: analysis-only`, so there's no arm to queue.

One thing I deliberately did not do: CI on `e2375a9794` is building now and I am not waiting on it. The PR is ready and the fold gates on the check itself, so if that build goes red the fold will hold it rather than the lane needing to sit here.
